clue.text: Humble saint, after a fashion

indicators.note: after places the saint's letters following the fashion word

parts.note: a mode is a fashion or style

explanation.surface: A holy person who is modest in a way, or after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a fashion' reads as a set phrase meaning 'somewhat', but it splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a humble person is unassuming and does not boast.

clue.text: Girl on mountain top to give less than a completely accurate account

definitions.text: give less than a completely accurate account

indicators.note: on puts the girl word above the mountain word in this down entry

parts.note: a miss is a girl
a peak is the top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A girl at a summit who is not telling the whole truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to say something wrongly or misleadingly is to misstate it.

clue.text: Two characters enjoy modern music — and a bit of Handel

parts.note: to dig is slang for to enjoy
rap is a modern style of music

indicators.note: a bit of here takes just the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A pair of people who like current music and a little classical Handel too.
explanation.definitionFit: Linguistics: a digraph is a pair of letters representing one sound, like sh.

clue.text: Magician using weird crosses without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the scrambled letters surround the hesitation
weird signals the letters are put in a strange new order

parts.note: er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A conjuror making strange crosses with no pausing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean minus, but it is the old sense of outside; 'weird' makes SORCESS, which goes round the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sorceress is a female practitioner of magic, a witch.

clue.text: Arrangement that keeps Rex in touch

indicators.note: keeps means the phrase for being in touch holds the king's letter within it

parts.note: to be in contact is to be in touch
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A deal that keeps a man called Rex in communication.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a contract is a formal agreement or deal between parties.

clue.text: In cursory comments old boy gets cattier somehow about princess

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: about means the scrambled letters go around the princess
somehow means the letters are arranged in some other way

parts.note: Di is Princess Diana

explanation.surface: A former schoolboy turns spiteful about a princess in offhand remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' makes ITERCTA, which 'about' wraps round the princess.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal Latin: obiter dicta are remarks made in passing, not essential to a judgment.

clue.text: Board of firm ousting leader

indicators.note: ousting leader means the first letter of the firm word is thrown out

parts.note: stable means firm, steady

explanation.surface: A company's board of directors pushing out its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' seems to be a company, but it means steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a table is a board, as in a board laid with food.

clue.text: Complain about a period of rule audibly

indicators.note: audibly signals that the words are to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a reign is a period of rule

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a monarch's time on the throne, out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to arraign is to criticise or formally accuse someone.

clue.text: Restriction when English Catholic enters church service

indicators.note: enters means the English and Catholic letters go inside the restriction word

parts.note: a tie is a restriction or bond
RC stands for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: A limit on an English Catholic going into church worship.
explanation.definitionFit: Liturgy: tierce, or terce, is the canonical office said at the third hour of the day.

clue.text: Sweet boy following you and me around

indicators.note: following puts the boy's name after the turned pronoun
around turns the two-letter pronoun backwards

parts.note: you and me together make us
Gary is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A sweet lad who tags along after the two of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sugary is very sweet, literally or in manner.

clue.text: Like one uplifted — as 'er with bra on, I fancy

indicators.note: fancy as a verb means imagine, signalling the letters are to be reimagined in a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a woman lifted up by her bra, as one might imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges ER, BRA, ON and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: something lifted into the sky and carried there is borne by the air.

clue.text: Map includes church with a Middle English geographical identification

indicators.note: includes means the map word takes the church letters inside it

parts.note: a plan is a map or diagram
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A map listing a church, with an old Middle English name for a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a place name identifies a geographical location such as a town or hill.

clue.text: Snail messes around, showing a lack of purpose

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A snail making a mess as it wanders about without direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being without a goal or direction is lacking any purpose.

clue.text: From Aberdeen I acquired an old computer

indicators.note: From signals the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone tells of picking up a vintage computer in Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: ENIAC was an early American electronic computer of the 1940s.

clue.text: Lady sins — a home broken — what's caused adultery?

indicators.note: broken means the letters of these words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A woman cheats, a household is wrecked, and the question is who is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ashley Madison is a website set up to arrange extramarital affairs, so it can be blamed for infidelity.

clue.text: Electronic chart conveyed in coastland signal

indicators.note: conveyed in means the electronic chart letters are carried inside the coast word

parts.note: the shore is land along the coast
a map is a chart

explanation.surface: A digital chart passing on a coastal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: semaphore is signalling with flags or arms, used at sea and on railways.

clue.text: Number engaged by nasty agency to produce toxic gas

indicators.note: engaged by means the number abbreviation is held within the scrambled letters
nasty signals the letters are spoilt and rearranged

explanation.surface: A figure hired by a sinister agency to make poison gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' makes CYAGEN, which is 'engaged by' the number abbreviation sitting inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry: cyanogen is a colourless, highly poisonous gas compound of carbon and nitrogen.

clue.text: Lazy, heartless, despotic man running a significant business

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of the word for idle is removed, leaving room for something else

parts.note: running means the letters of despotic man are set in motion and rearranged to fill the gap

explanation.surface: A description of an idle, cruel tyrant in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle from LAZY, and the gap is filled by DESPOTIC MAN rearranged, 'running' being the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a firm whose shares are traded on a stock exchange is usually a substantial enterprise.

clue.text: European secure after revolution, having grabbed a piece of electronic equipment

indicators.note: having grabbed means the turned securing word holds the other letters inside
after revolution means the securing word is turned backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to secure it
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Someone safe after an uprising who snatched a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after revolution' gives LIAN, which then 'grabs' the television set.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Latvian is a native of Latvia, a Baltic country in Europe.

clue.text: Going off with tot on to heather

indicators.note: on to puts the adding word above the heather word in this down entry

parts.note: to tot up is to add
ling is a name for common heather

explanation.surface: Taking a small child off over the heather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a child, but it is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an egg that is addling is going rotten, or going off.

clue.text: Employment in someone's home put on hold

indicators.note: in means the employment word sits inside the home word

parts.note: a pad is slang for one's home or flat
use is employment, as in putting to use

explanation.surface: A job working in a private house has been suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stopped temporarily, as a film or plan is put on hold.

clue.text: Battle one lost in part of London

indicators.note: lost means the letter for one is dropped from the fighting word

parts.note: action is fighting, a battle
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A battle in which one soldier was lost, fought in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton is a district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Acton is a district in the west of London.

clue.text: Badly-off American city flooded by rising river

indicators.note: flooded by means the city letters are filled with the river letters

parts.note: NY is New York

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the river name reads upwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: An impoverished American city swamped by a river in flood.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: needy people are poor, lacking money or necessities.

clue.text: Boy going around drunk, not having very good application

indicators.note: going around means the boy word wraps itself about the drinking word

parts.note: a son is a boy
lapped means drunk, as a cat laps milk

explanation.surface: A tipsy boy staggering about, not trying very hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: paint or make-up applied carelessly is put on hastily, without a good finish.

clue.text: Spit 'leek' out — it's a bit of grass

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: An instruction to spit out the word leek, which is a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany: a spikelet is a small flower cluster forming part of the head of a grass.

clue.text: Little woman and monarch fooling around

parts.note: Jo March is one of the sisters in the novel Little Women
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A small woman and a king clowning about together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' is not just a short female: it points to Jo in Alcott's Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be kidding is to be fooling around rather than serious.

clue.text: Affectedly elegant man tucked into food

indicators.note: tucked into means the man's name is placed inside the food word

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food
Andy is a man's name

explanation.surface: A smart chap with an affected air, eating his food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating heartily, but it means put inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dandy is a man vain about his clothes, so foppish manner fits.

clue.text: King's daughter enthralling a President once

indicators.note: enthralling means the daughter's name captures the letter inside it

parts.note: Regan is a daughter of King Lear in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A royal princess charming a former head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States.
